gap_1_link_tables.verdict: OPTION C - rebuild from flightlist bronze via T-08
gap_1_link_tables.rationale: raw_vault.py L158-199 builders drop day; monoliths cannot carry day. Option A (extend builders to emit day + regenerate monolith) is dead-column-everywhere and more code. Option B (join against hub_flight) consumes 3.5 GB RSS and adds single-shot code path. Option C deletes link monoliths, clears their watermarks, runs standard T-08 incremental pass; T-08's _partition_done gate skips the already-migrated tables and only writes link partitions per month via ym_from_filename -- byte-identical to fresh-pipeline output. ~165M rows total; minutes per month.
gap_1_link_tables.downstream_day_dependency: none. marts.build_fact_flight_for_ym joins link to hub_flight on hk_flight not day; sink/matrix never read day off link tables.

gap_2_sat_flight_summary.verdict: FILE-MONTH key (Option B) via bronze rebuild (Option C)
gap_2_sat_flight_summary.rationale_1_primary_source: raw_vault.py L543 (frame[ym] = pd.Series([ym] * len(frame), dtype='string') where ym = ym_from_filename(f.name)) confirms T-08 uses FILE-MONTH for all 4 partitioned flightlist-derived tables. T-11 APPROVED this writer on 2026-11-19. Dispatch's 'Option A matches T-08' is empirically wrong.
gap_2_sat_flight_summary.rationale_2_t15_adr: etl4/docs/decisions.md 2026-11-20 T-15 ADR tail entry explicitly states per-ym read scope means cross-month rows never share a frame inside build_fact_flight_for_ym; reader rule closes R1 only on multi-ym reads or future global reducer; operationally R1 is closed by sink UPSERT + rewind M+/-1 contract. Partition key choice is orthogonal to T-15 closure. Dispatch's 'Option B breaks T-15' misreads the ADR.
gap_2_sat_flight_summary.rationale_3_split_brain: Option A (firstseen migration key) would put 12,685 cross-month rows at firstseen-month (6,152 at ym=2022-05, 6,533 at ym=2022-11) while T-08's ongoing writer places them at file-month (ym=2022-06, ym=2022-12). Subsequent rewind+rebuild of 2022-06/2022-12 regenerates those 12,685 rows at file-month locations, leaving dead orphan rows at firstseen-month partitions. Permanent split-brain unless T-08 is also changed to firstseen -- which reopens T-08 and invalidates T-11 approval.
gap_2_sat_flight_summary.implementation: sat_flight_summary monolith = 4,600,646 rows across 2 months; rebuild via T-08 bronze pass is < 1 minute. Operator path identical to Gap 1: delete monolith, clear watermark, run incremental T-08.

gap_3_in_file_ym_and_done_sentinel.verdict: CONFIRMED - both additions are correct and binding; architecture section 6 is amended via patch text in review document section 4
gap_3_in_file_ym_and_done_sentinel.rationale_in_file_ym: architecture section 6.2 (committed) already states 'ym is retained in-file'; raw_vault.py L543 is the T-08 writer convention; without it, concurrent reads of migrated + T-08 partitions through vault_io.read_table would yield NaN for ym on migrated rows (Spark broadcast-join risk, fact_trajectory_enriched.ym backfill drift).
gap_3_in_file_ym_and_done_sentinel.rationale_done_sentinel: raw_vault.py L448 _write_done is the T-08 resume gate convention; L529 _partition_done checks for both part.parquet and _DONE. Without the sentinel, next T-08 run with cleared watermark would see part.parquet but no _DONE and either misread partition state or rebuild over the migrated partition, double-writing. Advisor caught this during T-12 implementation; dev-backend added it. Correct.
gap_3_in_file_ym_and_done_sentinel.sentinel_format: migration script writes 'load_dt=<iso>\nsource=migrate_partition_ym\n'; _partition_done tests existence only, so the extra provenance line is byte-safe.

operator_runbook_summary: Full runbook in t13_migration_review.md section 2. Key gates: (step 4) HARD GATE on vault_io.row_count == pre-migration footer for all 4 migrated tables BEFORE (step 5) monolith delete; (step 6) bronze rebuild of 3 flagged tables with watermark clear; (step 8) pre-rewind lock release only after step 7 row-count verification. Pre-rewind lock between steps 1 and 8 is MEDIUM severity operator-enforced constraint; rewind during the migration window would delete partitions the migration wrote and break the T-08 _partition_done skip optimization.
